assessment.nobel_worthiness: A transformative empirical programme that made intergenerational mobility measurable at population scale and reshaped research and public understanding of inequality of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: The proposed laureates are central to the linked administrative-data, measurement, and causal research programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated a durable research agenda, extensive follow-on evidence, and applications across places and policies.
uncertainties: The candidate framing spans a broad collaborative literature, making a three-person attribution necessarily incomplete.
Interpretation of geographic mobility patterns as policy mechanisms remains context dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work supplied a compelling framework and influential evidence on how trade and technology shocks reshape local labour markets, occupations, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are the clearest core contributors to the integrated empirical account of trade exposure and labour-market adjustment.
assessment.maturity: Its findings have been repeatedly examined, extended internationally, and remain foundational to research on labour-market adjustment.
uncertainties: Separating trade effects from concurrent technological and regional changes is empirically demanding.
The relative breadth of the technology and trade components complicates a single contribution label.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence methods made labour-market discrimination directly measurable at scale and established a major empirical approach with substantial societal importance.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are especially central to landmark correspondence evidence, while Charles represents the broader development of discrimination research.
assessment.maturity: The approach has accumulated extensive replications, methodological refinements, and applications in multiple countries and markets.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates identify differential treatment in specified settings but do not by themselves fully characterize all mechanisms of labour-market inequality.
Attribution across the large audit-study literature is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme established that early-life health and conditions can have lasting economic consequences, linking credible empirical evidence to a dynamic account of skill formation.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are central to evidence on early-life shocks, and Cunha to the dynamic human-capital framework connecting those findings.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is well developed across datasets, cohorts, and policy settings and has reshaped health, education, and labour research.
uncertainties: The contribution combines empirical and theoretical strands whose boundaries and relative credit are not sharp.
Long-run causal estimates can depend on setting-specific institutions and data coverage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on monopsony moved imperfect competition in labour markets from a peripheral possibility to a central organizing framework for wages, employment, and labour policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied foundational modern analysis; Naidu and Ashenfelter represent key theoretical and empirical development of the agenda.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become highly influential and has stimulated a large body of empirical work and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Empirical estimates of employer market power vary substantially by market definition and institutional setting.
The intellectual lineage extends beyond the proposed attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research made management practices measurable and connected organisational differences to productivity, diffusion, and economic performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are central architects of the measurement programme, with Sadun a major contributor to its extension and interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The work has been deployed across countries and firms, with a substantial follow-on literature and experimental evidence.
uncertainties: Survey-based measurement and selection into management practices complicate causal interpretation.
The contribution overlaps with a wider literature on organisations and productivity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research agenda made teacher effectiveness, school incentives, and educational production central empirical objects in economics and policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Hanushek, Kane, and Hoxby each made influential contributions to the measurement and analysis of school quality and accountability.
assessment.maturity: The questions, data, and methods have generated a large and persistent international literature.
uncertainties: The candidate combines several related but distinct contributions, weakening the unity of attribution.
Policy conclusions from teacher and school-effect estimates remain sensitive to design and context.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The construction and analysis of long-run income and wealth-distribution data profoundly changed the empirical study of inequality and offshore wealth.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez, and Zucman are central to the data-building and interpretive programme described.
assessment.maturity: The work has produced durable public datasets, extensive scholarly debate, and a broad subsequent research agenda.
uncertainties: Measurement of wealth, capital income, and offshore assets requires consequential assumptions and remains contested.
The broad historical programme includes important contributions by researchers outside the proposed group.
